body: Quick pass: merges cleanly with main; body complete; author's post suites, app lathe suites, clippy and quick gate green on f3c3c34a; no existing golden changed. Flagged ready; posted G-code, so it gets the high-tier review as soon as a reviewer slot frees.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f3c3c34a72012edd6c6c872ce9ae44044f008f64 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers found. This was a high-tier review: the PR changes posted G-code on the Fanuc lathe post.

### What looks good
- `endPreamble` (`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps:461-478`) now calls `afterOp()` once for every section. The live branch releases in this order: `M9`, `live_tool.spindle_off`, `live_tool.c_axis_off`, `G99`, then the asked words. So the driven tool is stopped and C is released before any `M00`/`M01`/`G28`.
- `afterAsk` is cleared inside `afterOp()`, which now runs for live sections whether or not they engaged. A refused live section uses up its own request and cannot carry it into the next section. `PARAM AfterOperation` arrives before `SECTION`, so a request can never be posted ahead of its own section.
- The live words are taken only from the machine file (`liveCodes` = `machine.liveTool`). M1001-M1004 appear only in the test fixture `millturn-live.mch`, not in the script.
- No existing golden changed. `git diff origin/main...f3c3c34a --stat -- crates/app/tests/golden crates/post/tests/recorded/golden` shows 11 files, all newly added `live_then_stop` files and no modified ones.

### Local results (trial-merged with origin/main 0fc30b65, merged cleanly)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (every suite, all 11 per-post suites included) | all green; script_fanuc_lathe 15/15, recorded_streams 12/12, post_engine 33/33, each other script_* 11/11 |
| app `lathe_post` / `lathe_post_css` / `lathe_post_tormach` / `lathe_post_refusals` | 7 / 10 / 8 / 11 passed |
| app `c_axis_live` / `c_axis_unwind` / `lathe_cycle_exit` | 5 / 7 / 6 passed |
| app `conformance` / `golden_cl` / `solid_law_goldens` / `recorded_post_streams` | 6 / 25 / 5 / 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**The pinning tests fail without the fix.** I put main's `fanuc-lathe.cps` back in the review worktree (local only, then restored). Four tests went red: `an_optional_stop_…`, `a_program_stop_…`, `a_go_home_…` and the `live_then_stop` golden. The negative `no_stop_asked_after_a_live_section_posts_no_stop` stayed green.

### Sequences I posted (local scratch test, not committed; test mill-turn; G00/G01/comments/T/G54 lines left out)
- **turning(stop) -> live -> turning:** `M9 | M05 | M00 | G98 | M1001 | M1003 S1200 | M8 | M9 | M1004 | M1002 | G99 | G97 S1300 M03 … M05 | G28 U0 W0 | M30`. The turning section's stop stays with that section, and the live section posts no stop.
- **turning -> live(stop) -> turning:** `… M9 | M1004 | M1002 | G99 | M00 | G97 S1300 M03 … M05 | G28 U0 W0 | M30`. On main this posted `… M05 | M00 | G28 U0 W0`, i.e. after the next section (the bug, reproduced).
- **turning -> live(opt stop) -> live(home) -> turning:** `M1004 | M1002 | G99 | M01 | G98 | M1001 | M1003 S1300 … M1004 | M1002 | G99 | G28 U0 | G28 W0 | G97 S1400 M03 … M05 | G28 U0 W0 | M30`. Each word is posted once, at its own section.
- **live(stop) as the last section:** `… M1004 | M1002 | G99 | M00 | G28 U0 W0 | M30 | %`.
- **live(home) as the last section:** `… M1004 | M1002 | G99 | G28 U0 | G28 W0 | M30 | %`. There is no doubled home (`homedAt` holds), and `M30` comes last. On main, the request in this case was dropped and only the program-end `G28 U0 W0` was posted.
- **CSS turning(home) -> live(stop) -> CSS turning(opt stop):** `G96 S200 M03 … M05 | G97 | G28 U0 | G28 W0 | G98 | M1001 … M1004 | M1002 | G99 | M00 | G96 S200 M03 … M05 | G97 | M01 | G28 U0 W0 | M30`. The #1183 `G97` after a CSS section is unchanged. A live section never sets `cssOn`, so it never writes `G97`, which is correct because it cannot be CSS.
- **No live section, no requests (turning + CSS):** output is unchanged in form, matching the untouched goldens.
- **Refused live section (no machine) with home, between turning(opt stop) and turning:** `M05 | M01 | G28 U0 | G28 W0 | G97 S1300 M03 | M05 | G28 U0 W0 | M30`, plus the warning naming the missing live_tool words. The refused section uses up its own request and the turning section keeps its `M01`. In the reverse case (refused live(stop), then turning(opt stop)), each word lands at its own section. A refused program is never released anyway.
- **Feed mode after a live section:** `G99` is back in force. The next turning section relies on it, since it states no feed mode of its own, which is correct. The next live section restates `G98`.
- **Two requests on one section:** this cannot happen. `AfterOperation` is a single enum (`crates/post/src/post/after_op.rs:21`), so a section carries at most one request.

### Other posts
- Every other `afterModes` post (fanuc, haas, heidenhain, mazak, sinumerik, doosan-dnm, tormach-lathe) has an `endPreamble` that always reaches `afterOp()`, with no early return after `if (!sectionOpen) return;`.
- Tormach, carvera and tormach-plasma refuse the request by name. The engine (`crates/post/src/post/engine.rs:151-160`) adds a counted warning, "asks an optional stop after it, but this post script does not declare afterModes", for any `PARAM AfterOperation` sent to a script without `afterModes`. All three new `.refusal` goldens show it. A stop request is never silently ignored on those posts.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **Is the home move safe?** The post does not check where the tool is when the home move starts. In the recorded cross drill the stream has already retracted to X24 (diameter), outside the part, before the section end. `G28 U0` first is a radial move outward, which is the safe direction out of a radial hole. An axial live drill whose stream ended inside the hole would be the same exposure the turning branch already has (X before Z). That exposure predates this PR, and the generators' exit retracts (`lathe_cycle_exit`) guard it.
2. **`spinRev` after a live section (predates this PR).** The live branch does not reset `spinRev` (`fanuc-lathe.cps:470-471`), while the turning branch does (`:476`). A live section only sets it if its path carries a reverse-hand thread, which does not happen today, so there is no reachable effect. Resetting it in both branches would be tidier in a later change.
3. `docs/decisions/1188-live-section-after-op.md` explains the release order and why. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1188`, and the subject follows conventional commits. `recorded_streams.rs` is now 346 lines.

### Only a real control can prove
- That the builder's actual live-tool and C-axis release codes complete (no in-position wait or brake confirmation missing) before `M00`/`M01`.
- That `G28 U0` / `G28 W0` with C released behaves as expected on the target control. The test words M1001-M1004 are placeholders.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
